answer.rationale: The 18% cost mandate is binding and the incumbent contract lapses in 14 days without auto-renewal. Memory c2 indicates the low-cost vendor already cut unit cost sharply with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing, so switching primary supply satisfies the cost mandate alone without adding a second source or extending term. Memory c4 suggests that if we were renewing, benchmarking would recover margin, but the mandate here is structural, not marginal. Pulling c1 to confirm whether incumbent stability was a real dependency or just convenience; if integration risk is material, a narrow guard-rail (single PO at quoted price, 30-day review window) keeps delivery risk bounded while the switch is executed. Deferring (c5) would re-create a month-to-month gap right at line pressure; adding a second source (c3) would spend the one decision slot without hitting the 18% cut alone. Total cost of ownership drops most cleanly by moving primary volume to the vendor whose quote already meets the mandate, with the incumbent retained only as fallback until next cycle.
